interpretations.scope_boundary: In scope: a single side-effect — on an order status transition INTO "SHIPPED", emit exactly one fire-and-forget email via the already-existing SendGrid client to the order's billing email using the "order-shipped" template, made idempotent so a given order's SHIPPED transition can never trigger a second send. The boundary stops hard at: this one channel (email), this one trigger (the →SHIPPED transition specifically, not other status changes), and this one template. Everything that would touch the request's critical path, add channels, or add user-facing surface is excluded. (Note: this code-forge repo is the preflight framework SOURCE — it contains no order/SendGrid application code; the deliverable here is the pinned behavior-spec/scope-guard artifact that holds this exact boundary for a downstream consumer build, since there is no order service to edit in-repo.)
surfaces_in_scope: The order status-update handler/service path — the existing transition logic where status becomes SHIPPED, as the trigger hook-point (observe the transition; do not change its semantics)
A new notification step/service that consumes the SHIPPED transition event and calls the existing SendGrid client (template 'order-shipped', recipient = order's billing email)
An asynchronous dispatch mechanism so the send is fire-and-forget and never blocks or fails the status-update response (queue/background task/post-commit async, not inline await)
An idempotency record keyed to the order + SHIPPED transition (e.g. a sent-marker / dedup key persisted) so a retry or duplicate transition never sends twice
Tests proving: send-on-SHIPPED, no-send on other transitions, non-blocking, and exactly-once under duplicate/retry
surfaces_out_of_scope: SMS notifications
Push notifications
In-app notifications
Any notification-preferences UI or settings surface
Emails for any status other than SHIPPED (no order-confirmed, delivered, cancelled, etc.)
Adding, configuring, or swapping the SendGrid client itself — the existing client is reused as-is
New email templates beyond the existing 'order-shipped' template
Making the email send synchronous/blocking or letting a send failure roll back or fail the status update
Recipient logic beyond the order's billing email (no CC/BCC, no per-user contact resolution)
Changing order status-transition semantics or adding new statuses
interpretations.core_behavior: On an order's status transitioning to SHIPPED, asynchronously send exactly one "order-shipped" email to the order's billing email via the existing SendGrid client, guarded by a persisted per-transition idempotency key so it can never send twice and never blocks the status-update request.

interpretations.scope_boundary: Hook a side-effect onto the order status-transition path so that exactly one "order-shipped" email is sent the first time an order enters SHIPPED; boundary stops at that single email send — no change to the status-update request's success/latency, no other channels, no preferences, no template authoring beyond referencing the existing 'order-shipped' template.

surfaces_out_of_scope: SMS, push, and in-app notification channels
Any notification-preferences UI or user opt-in/opt-out settings
Emails for any status other than SHIPPED (DELIVERED, CANCELLED, etc.)
Authoring/editing the 'order-shipped' SendGrid template content itself
Changing the SendGrid client's interface or swapping providers
Retry/dead-letter/observability infrastructure beyond what fire-and-forget minimally needs
Blocking, failing, or rolling back the status-update request if the email send errors

interpretations.scope_boundary: Exactly one outbound effect: a SHIPPED transition fires one idempotent 'order-shipped' SendGrid email to the billing email, off the request's critical path. Boundary is the order status-update write path's commit — I hook the post-commit point that detects a non-SHIPPED→SHIPPED transition and nothing else; no other status, channel, recipient, template, or UI is touched.

The existing SendGrid client wrapper — call it with the 'order-shipped' template and the order's billing email; no changes to the client itself
An idempotency record keyed on (order_id, SHIPPED-transition) — a persisted sent-marker (e.g. a notifications-sent table/column) checked-and-set so a retry/duplicate transition never re-sends

Boundary: it ends at "one email sent (or skipped because already sent) for this one transition" — it does not touch any other order status, any other channel, or any preference/config surface.
